previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, recurrent cellulitis, venous stasis ulcers, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for worsening left leg cellulitis that progressed despite prior antibiotic treatment. She presented with erythema, pain, cracked skin, and discharge from chronic ulcers, along with low-grade fevers and chills. IV vancomycin and ciprofloxacin were started, and wound culture grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Imaging showed soft tissue edema without abscess or deep vein thrombosis, and vascular studies revealed normal arterial flow. Due to persistent infection and poor response, she was transitioned to oral linezolid. A mild drug rash that developed after prior doxycycline use resolved spontaneously. She was discharged home on a four-week course of linezolid, iron supplementation, and oxycodone for pain, with instructions to stop tramadol due to interaction risk, discontinue compression devices until skin healing, and follow up for wound care, infectious disease, and colonoscopy for iron deficiency anemia.

Assessment and Plan: Mrs. ___ is a ___ y.o. woman with a

# Cellulitis: Patient presented with recurrent cellulitis in the 
setting of venous stasis and non-healing skin ulcers.  She had 
been on doxycycline for a cellulitis diagnosed in ___.  She 
was seen in ___ clinic one week ago- her lower extremity redness, 
swelling, and warmth were improved.  Given that, her doxcycline 
was discontinued at this appointment.  In addition, she has 
multiple antibiotic allergies and there was concern for 
resistance development with chronic use of antibiotics.  Patient 
has developed cellulitis when antibiotics have been discontinued 
in the past.  She has responded well to vancomycin and 
doxycycline in the past.  Wound cultures in ___ have grown 
enterococcus (?contaminant) sensitive to vanc.  In ___, 
cultures grew coag pos Staph aureus.  

While here, lower extremitiy films did not reveal evidence of 
subcutaneous emphysema that would be suggestive of a necrotizing 
process.  Leg films did not show any signs of septic joint.  
Orthopedic surgery evaluated the patient and did not found any 
evidence of knee joint infection.  Her cellulitis improved with 
IV vancomycin and her pain was controlled well with oxycodone.  
She remained afebrile with a normal WBC throughout the 
hospitalization.  Given her previous success with doxycycline, 
she was placed on oral doxycyline at discharge with plans to 
follow up with ID on ___ to determine duration of therapy.  She 
also has follow-up with her PCP (Dr. ___ on ___. 

# Left Knee Pain: Patient with painful left knee on weight 
bearing and flexion.  Knee films did not reveal evidence of 
septic involvement of the joint, there were some notable 
arthritic changes.  She was evaluated by orthopedics who felt 
her symptoms were most likely to be due to patellar bursitis, 
with some contribution from overlying cellulitis causing her 
discomfort.  Her ability to ambulate improved while here.  
Patient to follow up with orthopedics as an outpatient on 
___.

# Left Calf Pain: Concerning for DVT given history, inflammatory 
state and decreased mobility currently.  LLE ultrasound did not 
reveal DVT. Pain was likely due to overlying skin involvement.

# Rash:  She developed a flat erythematous rash (resembled 
urticaria) on day of admission.  There was no associated 
pruritis.  It began prior to IV clindamycin but after vancomycin 
(no rxn to vanc in the past).  Patient has had contact 
dermatitis in hospital in the past.  She also has had many skin 
reactions to meds including several antibiotics.  Her rash 
improved despite continuing the vancomycin.  Most likely, this 
was related to contact dermatitis, as she has had this during 
previous admissions.
 
# Lipodermatosclerosis/Venous Stasis Ulcers: Chronic, 
non-healing.  Likely contributing to recurrent cellulitis.  
Vascular previously recommended ace bandage, elevation.  
Recently diagnosed with lipodermatosclerosis.  Patient should 
use ACE wraps and pneumatic compression stalkings as tolerated.
   
# Anemia:  Chronic anemia, diagnosed with iron deficiency in 
past.  Has intermittent guaiac positive stools.  She is 
scheduled for colonoscopy as outpatient.  Hematocrit remained 
stable during this admission.
  
# Asthma: Stable during admission.  Continued on home albuterol. 
   

# Cardiac: History of hyperlipidemia, borderline hypertension, 
AS.  Home meds continued.  Patient kept on a heart healthy diet.

# Restless Leg Syndrome: Continued home mirapex.

# Chronic Pancreatitis: Stable, continued home medications  
 
# Depression/PTSD: Stable during admission.  Patient remained in 
good spirits.   

# Vit D/Calcium: Continued home vit D and calcium 
supplementation 

# Prophylaxis: PPI, pneumoboots, bowel regimen prn
